description: The German Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) keeps the national record of frequency usage rights for terrestrial broadcasting and distributes regularly updated transmitter data for VHF FM (UKW), digital radio (DAB) and digital television (DVB-T) to a closed user group (Geschlossene Benutzergruppe, GBG). Members receive the usage rights that are coordinated internationally and those still under coordination in Germany, in XML files whose structure is set out in public format descriptions for each service; the descriptions were last revised on 3 July 2025, when the field length of the transmitter station key changed in all three formats. Admission is by application with an information sheet and form. The public web page gives only the format descriptions. Coverage: Germany, all licensed terrestrial broadcast transmitters, updated regularly. Format and access: XML for approved members; XLS and XLSX format descriptions openly downloadable; free of charge as far as stated. Caveats: not open data, so general researchers may be refused; the publicly visible information is limited to the formats; public listings of transmitter sites come from operators such as Media Broadcast and Deutschlandradio, whose national DAB+ network had 193 sites in 2026. Simulation uses: inventory of broadcast transmitters for hazard exposure and power backup studies, and coverage and interference modelling of FM, DAB+ and DVB-T2 networks. Related records: the BNetzA EMF database lists transmitter sites with safety distances openly, the Swiss BAKOM transmitter layer is the open counterpart next door, and the ITU BR IFIC holds international registrations.
